newsitem.title: USA: Mexico GDP growing at over 3.0 pct, says Camdessus.
newsitem.headline: Mexico GDP growing at over 3.0 pct, says Camdessus.

text.p: Mexico's gross domestic product is currently growing at over three percent and should grow at an even higher rate next year, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said Thursday.
"In terms of growth, (Mexico's) economy is already rebounding," Camdessus said at a news conference ahead of next week's joint meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
"We can discuss how much it will be, but we are obviously at a growth rate over three percent at present and we will go higher next year," he added.
Camdessus said that the IMF was satisfied with Mexico's performance since the international financial community came to the country's rescue to salvage its economy early in 1995.
The $50 billion loan package, which included $17.8 billion from the IMF, helped the Mexican government avoid a meltdown after the badly botched peso devaluation of December, 1994.
According to Camdessus, that gigantic bet on Mexico was already paying off, not only with improved financial indicators but with a real economic recovery.
"The IMF continues to support Mexico and we are already working on a program that could serve as a framework for the growth of the Mexican economy in the coming years," he added.
Camdessus said that, like other countries in world, Mexico would have to work to stamp out corruption in order to consolidate its economy and its democracy.
"Naturally, the government is convinced of this," he said.
